model: AvatarPoser (Phase A: fit on Quest2 synthetic data, no vision)

metric_units.rot_error_deg: degrees (geodesic distance, global post-FK rotation, mean per joint, all 25 quest_humanoid joints)
metric_units.jitter_m_s3: m/s³ (mean jerk of predicted motion, no GT reference)
metric_units.foot_skate_cm_s: cm/s (weighted horizontal foot sliding while in contact, ground reference calibrated per-sequence -- see notes)
metric_units.gpen_mean_mm: mm (joint-position approximation, NOT mesh-vertex -- quest_humanoid has no mesh asset ported yet; ground reference calibrated per-sequence)
metric_units.gpen_rate: fraction of frames with any joint below the per-sequence ground reference (joint-position approximation)
metric_units.eg_mpjpe_mm: mm (same as pos_error_cm, in SimXR's units, for direct Table-5 comparison)
metric_units.success_rate: fraction of frames with head position <0.5m from GT (SimXR Table 5 definition)

notes: Position reconstruction anchors the predicted skeleton on the known head-tracked position (Head_trans_global), not oracle root/pelvis translation -- matches how a real deployed system would work (root/pelvis is never directly tracked).

success_rate is structurally near-100% for any reasonable static kinematic regressor anchored this way (head is ~6 kinematic hops from the anchor) -- NOT comparable to SimXR's success rate, which comes from a temporally-extended physics rollout that can compound errors/fail catastrophically over time. eg_mpjpe_mm/pos_error_cm is the position metric that's actually informative here.

gpen_* is a joint-position approximation (all 25 joint centers vs floor), not the true SMPL-H mesh-vertex method results/baselines/avatarposer_w40_baseline.json uses -- quest_humanoid has no mesh asset in this repo (Phase B work). Comparable to evaluate_phc_metrics.py's compute_gpen() approximation, not to the baseline JSON.

foot_skate_cm_s and gpen_* use a per-sequence empirical ground reference (each sequence's own GT minimum foot-joint height), not literal Z=0. Reason: quest_humanoid's leg chain ends at b_l/r_foot_twist, an ankle-twist auxiliary joint, not a toe/sole ground-contact joint like SMPL's L_Toe/R_Toe -- verified empirically that this joint never approaches Z=0 even during active walking (40 random test sequences: min height 0.046m, median 0.073m). Without this recalibration, foot_skate's H_THRESH=0.033 (tuned for SMPL's toe-at-the-floor convention) never triggers real contact detection, and gpen's Z<0 check almost never fires -- both were silently near-zero for this reason, not because the predicted motion is unusually clean.

SimXR's own Headset-only ablation (Table 5, extracted via AI web-fetch that also produced unrelated garbled filler text in the same response -- treat as a working reference, not verified ground truth): success 73.0%, Eg-mpjpe 118.9mm.
